q: Which key combination is commonly used to copy selected text in Windows?
x: Ctrl + C copies the selection. Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.

q: Which of the following is a feature of a spreadsheet program?
o: Playing music and video files from a disc
Editing pictures pixel by pixel on a canvas
Calculating values using formulas in cells
x: A spreadsheet arranges data in rows and columns and recalculates formulas automatically. Audio and image editing and compiling are done by other software.

q: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
x: Windows manages hardware and programs, so it is an operating system. Oracle is database software, Photoshop is an image editor and Skype is a messaging application.

q: Which software manages files, memory and running programs on a computer?
x: The operating system allocates memory, schedules programs and organises files. A compiler translates code, antivirus detects malware and a database stores data for applications.

q: The process of loading the operating system into memory when a computer is switched on is called:
x: Booting starts the machine and loads the OS from storage into RAM. Defragmenting rearranges disk files and compiling translates code.

q: Which of the following file extensions normally represents an image file?
x: JPG is a compressed image format. EXE is an executable program, TXT is plain text and MP3 is an audio format.

q: Which of the following is considered an "operating system" for mobile phones?
x: Android is designed for mobile devices. Linux Mint and Mac OS X are desktop systems, and MS-DOS is an old text-based PC system.

q: Which of the following is a function of an operating system?
o: Designing web pages for different users
Calculating the salaries of the staff
x: Managing memory, processes, files and devices are core tasks of an OS. The other tasks are done by application software.

q: The file `report.docx` is in the folder Marks, which is inside the folder School on drive D. What is the file's full path?
x: A path starts with the drive and lists each folder from the outermost inward, then the file name: D:, School, Marks, report.docx. Reversing School and Marks would put School inside Marks.

q: A file on the computer's hard disk is selected in File Explorer and the Delete key is pressed. Where does the file normally go?
o: To the Recycle Bin, from where it can be restored
To a hidden folder that only the administrator can open
It is erased at once and cannot be restored
To the clipboard, ready to be pasted elsewhere
x: Files deleted from a hard disk are moved to the Recycle Bin, so they can be restored until the bin is emptied. The clipboard holds cut or copied items, not deleted ones.

q: A file in folder P is selected, Cut, and then Pasted into folder Q. What is the result?
o: The file stays only in folder P
The file is now only in folder Q
The file is moved to the Recycle Bin
The file is now in both P and Q
x: Cut followed by Paste moves the file: it is removed from P and placed in Q. Copy followed by Paste would leave a copy in both folders.

q: In Windows, which tool is used to change settings such as user accounts, the mouse and the list of installed programs?
x: The Control Panel groups the system settings, including user accounts, devices and uninstalling programs. The Recycle Bin only holds deleted files.

q: Which of these is NOT a valid file name in Windows?
x: Windows does not allow the characters \ / : * ? " < > | in file names, so `result?.txt` is refused. Spaces, underscores, hyphens and digits are allowed, so `my notes.txt` is valid.

q: In a Windows file search, which pattern matches every file whose extension is .txt, whatever the length of its name?
x: The wildcard * stands for any number of characters, so `*.txt` matches every .txt file. The wildcard ? stands for exactly one character, so `?.txt` matches only one-letter names such as `a.txt`.

q: A student types in a word processor while music plays and a file downloads in the background. Which operating-system feature makes this possible?
x: Multitasking lets the OS run several programs at the same time by sharing the CPU and memory between them. Booting only loads the OS when the computer starts.

q: Which statement correctly compares MS-DOS and Windows?
o: MS-DOS uses icons and windows; Windows works only with typed commands
Both work only with typed commands and have no mouse support
Both are application programs that run on top of another OS
MS-DOS works with typed commands; Windows uses icons, windows and a mouse pointer
x: MS-DOS has a command-line interface where the user types commands, while Windows has a graphical user interface (GUI). The second option reverses the two.

q: A new printer is connected, but Windows cannot use it until a small program written for that printer is installed. This program is called a:
x: A device driver lets the OS communicate with a particular hardware device. The print spooler only queues print jobs; it still needs the driver to talk to the printer.

q: In Windows, the bar usually along the bottom of the screen that holds the Start button and buttons for running programs is the:
x: The taskbar shows the Start button and the open programs. The title bar is the top strip of each window that shows its name.

q: Windows is set to hide known file extensions. A file is shown as `photo.jpg`, but its real full name is `photo.jpg.exe`. What kind of file is it?
o: A program, because the real extension is .exe
A picture that has been compressed into a program
A text file, because extensions are hidden
A picture, because its name contains .jpg
x: Only the last extension decides the file type, and here it is .exe, so opening it runs a program; this trick is used to spread viruses. The .jpg is just part of the name.

q: Folder C:\Data contains two folders, X and Y. The file `f.txt` is inside X. The whole folder X is then moved into folder Y. What is the new path of `f.txt`?
x: Moving a folder moves everything inside it, so X keeps `f.txt` and X now sits inside Y, which is still inside Data. The path does not become C:\Data\Y\f.txt because X itself is moved, not emptied.

q: A desktop shortcut that points to the file `notes.docx` in the Documents folder is deleted. What happens to `notes.docx`?
o: It is deleted together with the shortcut
It stays where it is; only the shortcut is removed
It is moved from Documents to the desktop
x: A shortcut is only a link to the file, so deleting it does not touch the original. The file stays in Documents and can still be opened from there.

q: The Read-only attribute of a file is turned on. What does this mean?
o: It can be opened only by the administrator
It cannot be opened by any program at all
It is hidden and does not appear in the folder
It can be opened, but changes cannot be saved to it under the same name
x: A read-only file can be viewed but not overwritten; edited work must be saved under a new name. Hiding a file is a different attribute, Hidden.

q: Several programs are waiting to run, and the operating system decides which one gets the CPU next. This is part of which OS function?
x: Scheduling programs on the CPU belongs to process management. Memory management decides where in RAM each program is placed, not which one runs next.

q: The Delete key is used to delete one file from the hard disk C: and another file from a USB flash drive. Which statement is correct?
o: The file from C: goes to the Recycle Bin; the file from the USB drive is removed permanently
Both files go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored
Both files are removed permanently at once
The file from the USB drive goes to the Recycle Bin; the file from C: is removed permanently
x: Windows keeps a Recycle Bin for files deleted from the hard disk, but files deleted from a removable flash drive are not moved there. So only the file from C: can be restored from the bin.

q: What does the Format Painter do in a word processor?
o: Copies the formatting of selected text onto other text
Copies the selected text itself to another place
Changes the colour of the whole page background
Draws a picture inside the document
x: Format Painter copies formatting such as font, size and colour, and applies it to the text you select next; the words themselves are not copied. Copy and Paste is used to copy the text.

q: Which paragraph alignment lines the text up evenly with both the left and the right margins?
x: Justified text has straight edges on both sides because spaces between words are stretched. Centred text is placed in the middle with ragged edges on both sides.

q: In mail merge, the list of names and addresses that supplies a different value to each copy of the letter is called the:
x: The data source holds the records, one per recipient. The main document holds the text that is the same in every letter, with merge fields where the data goes.

q: A one-page letter is merged with a data source of 40 records. A filter is set so that only records with City = Lahore are included, and 12 records match. How many letters are produced?
x: Mail merge produces one letter for each record that is included, and the filter leaves 12 records, so 12 letters. 40 would be the count without the filter; 28 is the number of records left out.

q: In a mail-merge letter, what happens to a merge field such as «FirstName» when the letters are merged?
o: It is printed exactly as «FirstName» in every letter
It is replaced by the value from each record of the data source
It is deleted from every letter
It is replaced by the name of the data-source file
x: Each merge field is a placeholder: in each letter it is filled with that record's value, such as Ayesha in one letter and Bilal in the next. It is never printed as the field name in the merged result.

q: A school's name must appear at the top of every page of a 20-page report. Where should it be typed so that it appears on every page automatically?
x: Text in the header is repeated at the top of every page. The footer also repeats, but at the bottom of the page.

q: A note that explains one word, is linked to it by a small number and is printed at the bottom of the same page is called a:
x: A footnote appears at the bottom of the page where its number is. An endnote is also numbered, but all endnotes are collected at the end of the document.

q: In a table, two neighbouring cells in a row are selected and combined into one larger cell. This operation is:
x: Merging joins the selected cells into one. Splitting does the opposite: it divides one cell into several.

q: A table has 4 rows and 3 columns. One new row is inserted below row 2 and then one column is deleted. How many cells does the table have now?
x: Rows: 4 + 1 = 5; columns: 3 - 1 = 2; cells = 5 × 2 = 10. 15 would be the count before the column was deleted (5 × 3).

q: A table has 3 rows and 3 columns, all cells unmerged. Only the middle cell is split into 2 columns and 1 row. How many cells does the table have now?
x: Before the split there are 3 × 3 = 9 cells. One cell is replaced by 2, so 9 - 1 + 2 = 10. 11 would wrongly add 2 cells without removing the one that was split.

q: In the formula H₂O, the 2 is written smaller and lower than the letters. Which formatting is used for it?
x: Subscript lowers small text below the line, as in H₂O. Superscript raises it above the line, as in x².

q: Which setting changes the distance between the lines inside one paragraph?
x: Line spacing, such as single or double, sets the gap between lines of a paragraph. Indentation moves the paragraph in from the margin but does not change the gap between lines.

q: Only the first line of each paragraph should start 1 cm further in than the other lines. Which setting does this?
x: A first-line indent moves just the first line inward. A hanging indent does the opposite: the first line stays out and the following lines are moved in.

q: A table with many wide columns does not fit across an A4 page. Which page setting gives the most width for the table without making the text smaller?
x: Landscape turns the page sideways, so the longer side runs across and there is more width. Portrait is the normal upright page with less width.

q: A document contains the line "The cat sat on a category list." Replace All is used to replace cat with dog, with Match case and Find whole words only both turned off. What does the line become?
o: The dog sat on a dogegory list.
The cat sat on a dogegory list.
The dog sat on a dog list.
The dog sat on a category list.
x: With whole words off, every place where the letters cat appear is changed, including inside category, giving dogegory. The second option would be the result only if Find whole words only were on.

q: The correctly spelled name Qasim is shown with a red wavy underline while typing. What is the most likely reason?
o: The sentence has a grammar mistake
The word has been made into a hyperlink
The word is not in the program's dictionary
The word is formatted as hidden text
x: The spell checker underlines any word it cannot find in its dictionary in red, even a correct name; it can be added to the dictionary. A red wavy line marks spelling, not grammar.

q: A word that is not bold is selected and Ctrl+B is pressed two times. How does the word look now?
o: It is not bold, as it was at the start
x: Ctrl+B switches bold on and off: the first press makes the word bold and the second press removes it. Underline and italic are set by other commands.

q: Which word-processor tool suggests other words with the same meaning, such as "big" for "large"?
x: A thesaurus lists synonyms. The spell checker only checks whether words are spelled correctly.

q: While typing a long paragraph, a student never presses Enter at the end of a line, yet the text moves to the next line by itself at the right margin. This feature is called:
x: Word wrap carries words that do not fit onto the next line automatically; Enter is needed only to start a new paragraph. AutoCorrect fixes common typing mistakes.

q: Each chapter of a report must start at the top of a new page, even after more text is added to the previous chapter. What should be placed before each chapter heading?
o: Several empty lines made with Enter
x: A page break always pushes the following text to a new page. Empty lines made with Enter move when text above them grows, so the heading can end up in the middle of a page.

q: An automatic numbered list has 5 items numbered 1 to 5. Item 3 is deleted. What number does the last item show now?
x: Automatic numbering renumbers the remaining items, so the four items left are numbered 1 to 4. A typed-in number would have stayed 5, but this list is automatic.

q: A table has the rows (Ali, 72), (Sara, 91), (Bilal, 64) and (Hina, 80). It is sorted by the marks column in descending order. Whose row is third?
x: Descending order puts the largest first: Sara 91, Hina 80, Ali 72, Bilal 64. So Ali is third. In ascending order (64, 72, 80, 91) the third row would be Hina instead.

q: A student opens the file `essay.docx`, edits it and, without saving first, uses Save As to save it as `essay2.docx`. What is in `essay.docx` on the disk now?
o: Nothing, because the file was deleted
The text as it was before the edits
The edited text, the same as essay2.docx
x: Save As writes the edited document to the new file and leaves the old file as it was last saved. Only Save would have written the edits into `essay.docx`.

q: Cells A1, A2 and A3 hold 4, 7 and 9. What does the formula `=SUM(A1:A3)/A1` show?
x: SUM(A1:A3) = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20, and 20 / 4 = 5. 13.25 comes from `=A1+A2+A3/A1`, where only A3 is divided because division is done before addition.

q: Cells B1 to B4 hold 6, (empty), 9 and 3. What does `=AVERAGE(B1:B4)` show?
x: AVERAGE ignores empty cells, so it averages 6, 9 and 3: 18 / 3 = 6. 4.5 is 18 / 4, which wrongly counts the empty cell.

q: Cells C1 to C5 hold 5, the text Ali, 8, (empty) and 0. What does `=COUNT(C1:C5)` show?
x: COUNT counts only cells that contain numbers: 5, 8 and 0, so 3. Zero is a number and is counted; 2 forgets it, and 4 wrongly counts the text.

q: Cells A1 to A4 hold 12, 5, 20 and 9. What does `=MAX(A1:A4)-MIN(A1:A4)` show?
x: MAX = 20 and MIN = 5, so 20 - 5 = 15. 25 adds them instead of subtracting.

q: Cell B2 holds 50. What does `=IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")` show?
x: The test 50 >= 50 is true, so IF shows its second argument, Pass. Fail would be shown only if the test were B2 > 50.

q: Cell A1 holds 80. What does `=IF(A1>80,"High",IF(A1>60,"Mid","Low"))` show?
x: 80 > 80 is false, so the inner IF runs; 80 > 60 is true, so it shows Mid. High would need A1 greater than 80, not equal to it.

q: What value does the formula `=2+3*4^2` show?
x: Excel does ^ first, then *, then +: 4^2 = 16, 3*16 = 48, 2 + 48 = 50. 80 comes from working left to right as (2+3)*16.

q: Cell C1 holds `=A1+B1`. It is copied and pasted into C2. Which formula is in C2?
x: Relative references move by the same amount as the cell: one row down, so A1 becomes A2 and B1 becomes B2. The columns stay the same because the copy stayed in column C.

q: Cell D2 holds `=B2*C2`. It is copied and pasted into E3. Which formula is in E3?
x: From D2 to E3 is one column right and one row down, so B2 becomes C3 and C2 becomes D3. =B3*C3 shifts only the rows and forgets the column move.

q: Cell B2 holds `=A2*$E$1`. It is copied down to B5. Which formula is in B5?
x: A2 is relative, so moving three rows down makes it A5; $E$1 is absolute and does not change. =A5*$E$4 would be the result only without the $ signs.

q: Cell C3 holds `=$A3*B$1`. It is copied and pasted into D5. Which formula is in D5?
x: The copy moves one column right and two rows down. In $A3 the column is fixed and the row changes: $A5. In B$1 the row is fixed and the column changes: C$1. So =$A5*C$1.

q: A1, A2 and A3 hold 10, 20 and 30, and E1 holds 2 (E2 and E3 are empty). B1 holds `=A1*$E$1` and is filled down to B3. What does B3 show?
x: Filled down, B3 holds =A3*$E$1 = 30 × 2 = 60, because $E$1 does not change. Without the $ signs, B3 would hold =A3*E3, and the empty E3 counts as 0, giving 0.

q: F1 holds a discount rate. B2 holds `=A2*F1` and gives the right answer, but after copying it down to B3:B6 those cells all show 0. What is the problem?
o: The values in column A must be typed as text
A formula cannot be copied to more than one cell
The multiplication sign must be x instead of *
F1 changed to F2, F3 and so on, which are empty; it should be $F$1
x: Copying down changes the relative reference F1 to F2, F3..., which are empty and count as 0. Writing $F$1 keeps every copy pointing at the rate cell.

q: How many cells are in the range A1:C4?
x: A1:C4 covers columns A, B, C (3 columns) and rows 1 to 4 (4 rows), so 3 × 4 = 12 cells. 7 adds the columns and rows instead of multiplying.

q: A1 holds 5 and A2 holds 10. Both cells are selected and the fill handle is dragged down to A5. What does A5 show?
x: Two selected values set a series with a step of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 in A1 to A5, so A5 is 25. 20 is the value in A4, one cell short.

q: What is the address of the cell in the 4th column and the 7th row of a worksheet?
x: A cell address is the column letter then the row number. The 4th column is D, so the cell is D7; G4 would be the 7th column and 4th row.

q: A1 and A2 hold numbers. Which entry typed into A3 will be calculated by Excel as a formula?
x: A formula must begin with an equals sign. Without it, A1+A2 is just stored and shown as text.

q: A1 holds 12 and B1 holds 0. What does `=A1/B1` show?
x: Dividing by zero is impossible, so Excel shows the error #DIV/0!. #NAME? appears for a misspelled function name, not for division by zero.

q: A cell that holds a long number shows ##### instead of the number. What is the usual cause?
o: The column is too narrow to show the number
The number has been stored as text
The formula in the cell has a spelling error
The cell has been locked by a password
x: Excel fills the cell with # signs when a number does not fit the column width; widening the column shows it. A number stored as text is shown as typed, not as #####.

q: Which chart type is best for showing what share of a single total each item has, such as each subject's part of a student's total marks?
x: A pie chart shows each value as a slice of one whole, so shares are easy to compare. A line chart is meant for change over time.

q: A column chart was made from the marks in B2:B6. The value in B4 is then changed from 40 to 70. What happens to the chart?
o: It keeps showing 40 until it is made again
It is deleted because its data changed
It turns into a line chart
Its bar for B4 grows to 70 automatically
x: A chart is linked to its data range, so changing a cell redraws the chart at once. It does not have to be created again.

q: What is the relationship between a workbook and a worksheet in Excel?
o: A worksheet is a file that contains several workbooks
A workbook is a file that contains one or more worksheets
A workbook is one single cell of a worksheet
They are two names for exactly the same thing
x: An Excel file is a workbook, and it holds one or more worksheets (sheets) made of rows and columns. The second option reverses the two.

q: G1 holds 40. D2 holds `=IF(C2>=$G$1,"Pass","Fail")` and is filled down to D4. C2, C3 and C4 hold 39, 40 and 55. How many of D2:D4 show Pass?
x: Each copy compares its own row with the fixed $G$1 = 40: 39 >= 40 is false (Fail), 40 >= 40 is true (Pass), 55 >= 40 is true (Pass), so 2. 1 would forget that 40 equals the limit.
